text: For adults, a safe general activity target is at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-intensity aerobic activity, or an equivalent amount of vigorous activity, plus muscle-strengthening activities on at least 2 days per week. Activity can be spread across the week and broken into smaller sessions.

Adults who sit a lot should be encouraged to move more and sit less. Some physical activity is better than none, and even small increases in moderate or vigorous activity can provide health benefits when built up gradually.

A healthy diet should emphasize a variety of minimally processed foods such as vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes, and nuts. General lifestyle advice should also encourage moderation and diversity rather than extreme restriction.

Healthy eating patterns should limit excess salt or sodium, free sugars, saturated fat, and trans fat. For lifestyle recommendations, this supports advice such as reducing sugary drinks, salty takeout, fried foods, and highly processed snacks.

Healthy weight management should focus on a specific, sustainable plan that combines healthy eating patterns, regular physical activity, enough sleep, and stress management. Gradual weight loss is safer and more sustainable than rapid weight loss, so recommendations should avoid extreme dieting or unrealistic short-term promises.

source_title: Get the Facts: Sugar-Sweetened Beverages and Consumption
text: Sugar-sweetened beverages are major sources of added sugars. Frequently consuming sugary drinks is associated with weight gain, obesity, type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and other health risks, so lifestyle advice can suggest replacing them with water or unsweetened options.

For people with high blood pressure or hypertension risk, lifestyle guidance should emphasize a healthy eating pattern, healthy weight, regular physical activity, not smoking, limiting alcohol, and enough sleep. Users with hypertension should be encouraged to work with a healthcare professional, especially before major lifestyle or exercise changes.

Too much sodium can raise blood pressure, and limiting sodium is especially important for people with high blood pressure. Practical advice can include reducing packaged and restaurant foods, choosing lower-sodium options, and increasing potassium-rich foods when appropriate under professional guidance.

Quitting smoking can improve health at any age and reduce risks for cardiovascular disease, COPD, cancer, and premature death. For a user who smokes, health recommendations should include supportive smoking cessation advice and suggest evidence-based professional resources rather than judgmental language.

Excessive alcohol use increases health risks. Adults who drink can reduce risk by drinking less or not drinking; moderate drinking is defined as up to 2 drinks per day for men and up to 1 drink per day for women, but some people should not drink at all, including pregnant people and those with certain medical conditions or medication interactions.

source_title: National Diabetes Prevention Program: Lifestyle Change Program
text: For people with prediabetes risk, a structured lifestyle change approach can help prevent or delay type 2 diabetes. Core lifestyle targets include healthier eating, regular physical activity, and modest weight loss when appropriate, such as 5% to 7% of body weight and about 150 minutes of activity per week.

Adults generally need at least 7 hours of sleep per night. Better sleep habits include keeping a consistent sleep schedule, making the bedroom quiet and relaxing, turning off electronics before bedtime, avoiding large meals and alcohol before bed, limiting afternoon or evening caffeine, and exercising regularly.

For people with joint pain or mobility limitations, physical activity should be joint-friendly and cause no or little pain. Lower-impact options can include brisk walking, cycling, light gardening, dancing, tai chi, swimming, and water exercises, with difficulty increased gradually over time.

When a user reports pain during an activity, recommendations should avoid pushing through pain or prescribing high-impact exercise. Safer advice is to choose activities that cause little or no pain, start with short sessions, increase gradually, and seek medical or physical therapy guidance if pain persists or worsens.

source_title: Tips for Healthy Eating for a Healthy Weight
text: A healthy eating plan for weight management can include fruits, vegetables, whole grains, low-fat or fat-free dairy, and a variety of protein foods such as seafood, lean meats, eggs, legumes, soy products, nuts, and seeds. It should be lower in added sugars, sodium, saturated fats, trans fats, and cholesterol.
